clues.text: This city stands where the plains run up to the Rocky Mountains. Two small creeks flow through it, at the north end of a long mountain front.
clues.narrowing: Points to the north end of the Rocky Mountain front, on the high plains.

source.quote: Cheyenne is the northern terminus of the extensive Southern Rocky Mountain Front.

clues.text: Winter cold here keeps breaking in a warm rush of wind. Chinook winds pour down from the peaks and lift some winter days past 50 degrees.
clues.narrowing: Rules out steady cold towns; keeps windy plains towns warmed by chinook winds.

source.quote: the cold is often interrupted, with chinook winds blowing downslope from the Rockies that can bring warm conditions

clues.text: A railroad crew laid out this town in 1867, and the first train rolled in that same year. In 1869, a new governor named it the territory capital.
clues.narrowing: Cuts the list to a railroad town named territory capital in 1869.

source.quote: Territorial Governor John Allen Campbell arrived in Cheyenne on May 7, 1869, and named Cheyenne the temporary territorial capital.

clues.text: Each summer, this city throws Frontier Days, a huge rodeo and Old West party. It is the best known show in town, and crowds pack in for it.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital hosts a famed Frontier Days rodeo each year.

source.quote: is known for the annual Cheyenne Frontier Days, a longstanding rodeo and cultural event

clues.text: The governor of Wyoming works in this city. State lawmakers meet here, in the seat of state rule.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the governor and state lawmakers work in this city.

source.quote: is the capital and most populous city of the U.S. state of Wyoming

reveal.blurb: The railroad laid out this town in 1867 beside a fort built to guard the tracks. Two years later it was named the territory capital, and it has held the seat ever since. Cheyenne is the capital of Wyoming.
